meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh, come on, Dad!
Well?

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
That's it, bye!

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дыхать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to rest, relax', paired with 'отдохнуть'.

examples.trans: Everything is great, get some rest!
In the summer we vacation by the sea.

examples.text: Всё отлично, отдыхай! Сегодня выходные, всё круто!
examples.trans: Everything is great, get some rest! It is the weekend today, everything is cool!

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'blood pressure' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He has high blood pressure.
Those make your blood pressure rise.

examples.text: Давление? Ничего, от тебя у меня просто кружится голова.
examples.trans: Blood pressure? It's nothing, you just make my head spin.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?
Where is your room?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'over, above; at', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The lamp is above the table.
Don't laugh at me.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'стаканить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to settle, sort out (colloq.)'.

examples.trans: We need to stabilize your blood pressure.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет устаканить без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to settle without a reason.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How was it in Hungary?
As you all know...
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'little window, serving hatch' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Climbing out the window like that.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новое окошко.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new little window.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
I'm doing my homework.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very, very much', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.
It's very hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

просить.gloss: to ask, to request, to beg

meanings.en: to ask, to request, to beg
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask, to request, to beg', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.
Samsonov, I asked you not to!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Good evening!
I'll call in the evening.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'глянуть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to drop in, peek in'.

related.gloss: not to to drop in (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Я вечером загляну еще, сейчас чайку вам принесу.
examples.trans: I will check in again this evening, and right now I will bring you some tea.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет заглянуть без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to drop in without a reason.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'more; still; yet', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You've still got some.
You'll be sorry!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'some tea' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Chef, do you want to drink some tea?
Having some tea, Viktor Petrovich?
Boss, more tea.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will bring', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.

examples.text: А что это ты в квартиру принёс?
examples.trans: And what is that you brought into the flat?

examples.text: Видишь, Аркаша, он собаку принёс тебе.
examples.trans: See, Arkasha, he brought you a dog.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.
How are things?

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
He's at our place.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'держать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to detain; to delay', paired with 'задерживать'.

examples.trans: The mayor has been detained.
I was held up at work.
The town's mayor, Arkady Anikeev, has been detained.

при.gloss: in the presence of, by, at

meanings.en: in the presence of, by, at
meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in the presence of, by, at', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The child isn't to blame.
And what does Lyolya have to do with it?

examples.text: Всё, я ухожу. Ребёнок ни при чём. Передай это Алексею.
examples.trans: That's it, I'm leaving. The child isn't to blame. Give this to Alexei.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пытка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'attempt' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Is this an attempt to stop me?

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть попытка.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always attempt.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.
I'm going to Mum's.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'flight, escape' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Detained while attempting to escape.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новое бегство.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new flight.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
Dad is already home.
I'm already home.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.trans: I don't know.
As you all know...

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'came', paired with 'приезжать'.

examples.text: Вика, ты на какой машине сегодня приехала?
examples.trans: Vika, which car did you come in today?
Why did you even come here? Empty-handed!

examples.text: Так, успокойтесь все. Сейчас за мной приедут.
examples.trans: Right, everyone calm down. They're coming for me any minute.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'везти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning '(they) delivered, brought', paired with 'привозить'.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
I've brought you your things.

examples.text: Плохой бетон привезли. Самсон, ты зря радиаторы носил.
examples.trans: They've delivered bad concrete. Samson, you carried those radiators for nothing.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to run around'.

related.gloss: not to to run around (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Это она со мной познакомилась! Вокруг меня бегала.
examples.trans: She was the one who came up to me! She was running after me.
She was running after me.

examples.text: Во время экскурсии не кричать и не бегать!
examples.trans: During the tour, no shouting and no running!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to jump, to hop in', paired with 'прыгнуть'.

examples.trans: Let's go! Jump in!
The children are jumping in the courtyard.

examples.text: Ну ты посмотри, какая машина! Поехали! Прыгай!
examples.trans: Just look what a car! Let's go! Jump in!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Grab him!
It needs a wash.
Four-eyes! Grab him!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such, like this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is this?
He's so kind.
Pavel Yuryevich, what is this?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'appetite' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Enjoy your meal!
He has a good appetite.
Your porridge. Enjoy your meal.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('Russian').

examples.trans: Samson, are you Russian?
I speak Russian.
Russian. Orthodox. Never been in prison.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'language; tongue' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I told you in plain Russian.
He knows the Russian language well.

examples.text: А ты не кричи на меня! Я тебе русским языком сказала.
examples.trans: Don't you yell at me! I told you in plain Russian.

выучить.gloss: to learn (by heart or thoroughly), to memorise

meanings.en: to learn (by heart or thoroughly), to memorise
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'учить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to learn (by heart or thoroughly), to memorise', paired with 'учить'.

examples.trans: And I've learned everything.
I learned all the new words.

examples.text: А я всё выучила. Я хорошо учусь.
examples.trans: And I've learned everything. I do well at school.
